Subject: Roadmap readout: dependency triage + launch controls

Team —

As we get QBR materials in shape, I want a focused readout on the product + infra launch slate we’ll present to the execs. I’m asking for a short dependency-and-risk triage so we don’t get surprised in the review.

Ask (deliverables by end of day Mon, Aug 31):
- A one-page risk snapshot per area (Product / Infra / Integrations) using the attached template (qbr_risk_template.xlsx). Use traffic light (Green/Amber/Red) + one-line mitigation and owner.
- Call out any hard launch blockers and an explicit rollback/mitigation control for each.
- For infra items, include estimated impact window (latency or throughput hit) and a feasible canary plan.

I’m specifically worried about two items I’ve seen in the last week: integration churn with Acme APIs and a recent memory pressure pattern on the low-latency path. If either is amber/red, include a proposed contingency (e.g., smaller model fallback, temporary routing rules).

I’ll consolidate everything into the QBR pack on Tue morning. Short readout in the Exec Prep channel at 10:00 PT on Wed (Sept 2) — please be prepared to present 60s each.

Thanks —
Vivek
Vivek Kulkarni
Head of Product Operations, Redwood Inference

Thanks Vivek — attaching a first cut (qbr-risk-matrix.xlsx). High-level notes:

- Product: New permutations UI is amber. Two known issues: (1) pagination regression on long lists (P1, fix in PR; needs qa signoff), (2) telemetry gap for new feature flags (we can add a temporary event). Mitigation: ship feature-flagged; hard cutoff date for on by Sept 7. Owner: Laura.

- Integrations: Acme API changes are listed in a separate sheet. Looks like they plan a deprecation window starting Sept 3 (Anna confirms below) — that’s a potential blocker for our scheduled Sept 6 launch. Owner: Karthik to coordinate smoke test.

- Infra: flagged as amber pending Marcus’ input on the memory pressure note.

Questions / asks:
1) What’s the acceptable SLA impact threshold for a canary before we escalate to an exec hold? Recommend 5% p95 latency increase or 10% throughput reduction.
2) Do we want an explicit fallback to the smaller model family as a protected control? (I think yes for customer-facing tiers.)

I attached the matrix and a diagram I sketched for dependencies (launch-deps-diagram.png).

Subject: Re: Roadmap readout: dependency triage + launch controls

Vivek / all —

Adding technical context on the memory-pressure observation: we saw repeated heap-pressure spikes in the prefix-cache worker pool under the high-concurrency synthetic tests (INF-4521). Root cause looks like a regression in the mem-evict path introduced in the batching refactor (PR #2987).

Impact: worst-case p95 latency +12-18% and occasional OOM exits for a small subset of small-instances during 60s bursts. Probable to affect customers at top QPS percentiles.

Mitigation options (short list):
- Hotfix: revert the mem-evict change and deploy v0.9.3. Estimated time: 2–3 hours to land + 1 hour of canary verification. (Owner: Marcus)
- Operational: temporary conservative batch size config to reduce memory footprint for affected pools (no code change). Can be toggled per pool. (Owner: Ops)
- Contingency: route high-QPS customers to a larger instance type for 24–72 hours if we see repro in org-level smoke tests. (Owner: Karthik for coordination)

I recommend the hotfix + conservative batch config during canary. We should reserve a 4-hour maintenance window (low traffic predicted Sat night PDT). If execs prefer zero-risk, we can gate launch until the hotfix is verified.

References: JIRA INF-4521, PR #2987. I attached a short rollback-runbook-draft.md to this thread.

Hi Karthik / Vivek —

Quick confirmation from Acme side: we have a planned deprecation for the legacy payload field on Sept 3 at 00:00 UTC. We will freeze any backwards-incompatible changes on Sept 2 at 16:00 PT to give partners a final integration window.

We can offer a 45-minute integration smoke test slot on Sept 2 at 18:00 PT (limited to two test clients). If Redwood needs an earlier slot, we may be able to rearrange.

If you are planning to rely on the legacy field for fallbacks, please call it out explicitly and we’ll keep it stable for that partner cohort through Sept 9 under a short-term bridge extension.

—Anna

Date: Wed, 01 Sep 2026 16:30:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Roadmap readout: dependency triage + launch controls — actions and alignment

Thanks all for fast turn-around. Consolidation below — please treat this as the single source of truth for the QBR pack and pre-read:

1) Owners and deliverables (due Tue morning, Sept 7:00 PT deck cut):
- Product risk snapshot (Laura) — finalize amber/green rows + one-line mitigation. Attached: qbr-risk-matrix.xlsx (final).
- Integration smoke tests (Karthik) — claim the Sept 2 18:00 PT slot with Acme; coordinate test clients and runbook. Add test results to the Exec Prep doc.
- Infra hotfix (Marcus) — land v0.9.3 hotfix in canary on Sept 1 22:00 PT; toggle conservative batch config for edge pools during canary. Ops to reserve 4-hr maintenance window.
- Rollback/runbook (Marcus + Ops) — publish rollback-runbook-draft.md and final sign-off by Sept 2 09:00 PT.

2) Controls we’ll present to execs:
- Canary thresholds: escalate to exec hold at >5% p95 latency or >10% throughput degradation (Laura agreed).
- Fallback: enable smaller-model routing for customer-facing tiers for immediate rollback. (Karthik to enable toggle.)
- Integration bridge: Acme will keep legacy field stable for our cohort through Sept 9 if we declare dependency; we should avoid relying on it beyond Sept 9.

3) Risks that may change the launch window:
- Any failure to complete the hotfix verification by Sept 2 end-of-day will move launch to a contingency window.
- If Acme cannot provide a successful smoke test on Sept 2, we will postpone customer-facing launch until Sept 10.

4) Meeting cadence: 30-min alignment on Sept 2 at 10:00 PT (Exec Prep channel) — 60s readouts from owners, then we’ll run through slides.

Please update the Drive pack and mark items as DONE in the Exec Prep checklist when complete. I’ll circulate a trimmed pack to the execs Tue 08:00 PT.

Thanks — appreciate the quick coordination.

Vivek
Vivek Kulkarni
Head of Product Operations, Redwood Inference
